chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Farrā', from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) who said:

Whoever is pleased with the Divine Decree, the Decree will come to him while he is rewarded; and whoever is displeased with the Divine Decree, the Decree will come to him and God will cancel his reward.

key_terms.رَضِيَ: To be pleased or content with
key_terms.سَخِطَ: To be displeased or discontent with

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in reward between being pleased and displeased with God's decree?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq to distinguish between passive resignation and active spiritual contentment (rida) regarding divine decree. The text emphasizes that one's internal disposition toward God's will determines whether the inevitable occurrence of destiny (al-qadā') becomes a source of merit or a cause for the nullification of good deeds. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the heart's alignment with divine wisdom as a key component of faith.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-80 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Ayoob ibn Nooh, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Al-Fura that Aba Abdullah Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “

What is destined will happen to whoever is pleased with his destiny, and he will be rewarded. However, what is destined will happen to whoever is displeased with his destiny but God will cancel his reward.”
